rows.notes: The study is a narrative review/position paper on sustainable water management; it reports no new data of its own. The list of improvements to localized irrigation (single drip line, micro-sprayers, duration adjustment, pressure control, filters, maintenance, automation) in Sections 3.1 and 4 is asserted without any experiment. Table 1 (kiwi WUE under drip vs sprinklers) is reproduced from a previously published study (Chartzoulakis et al., 1991), not reported as a result of this paper, and does not test the listed improvements.

Review/opinion paper with no primary data. The statement that the listed improvements to localized irrigation increase water productivity is a recommendation (Sections 3.1 and 4), not an own result. Table 1 is taken from Chartzoulakis et al. (1991) and shows no yield difference among drip, micro-sprinkler and overhead sprinkler in kiwi (all 'a'), so it would not even support a yield boost for drip.

Review/opinion paper. The passage on water pricing policy (Section 4) recommends volumetric metering, progressive/seasonal/over-consumption tariffs and drought surcharges as contributing to water savings; this is a policy recommendation with no data, survey or model run reported by the authors.

notes: The cited document is a conference review/overview paper (IRLA2014 proceedings) synthesising literature and offering recommendations. The only tabulated results (Tables 1 and 2) are reproduced from the first author's earlier publications (1991, 1992) and are not presented as results of this study. Text appears complete.
